verified.exploit_entry_point: Action execution through the executor chain (Executor.ExecRequest), reached from the StartAction / StartActionAndWait API, from webhooks and from triggers. The tests drive ExecRequest exactly as the project's own executor tests do (DefaultExecutor(cfg) + FindBindingWithNoEntity + ExecRequest + wait), with no stubs; the action runs a real sh/exec. The attacker inputs are the caller's identity (login name and group line, as set by the trusted-header / token / OAuth2 layer) and client-supplied argument maps.
variants: base (published fix, pattern A, the lead): the caller's login name is identity-derived and is placed into the shell command OliveTin runs without a type check, so shell metacharacters in the name execute (command injection in the main command).

base (published fix, pattern A): an undeclared client-supplied argument whose name carries the reserved system prefix survives the argument allowlist and is delivered into the command environment (allowlist bypass). A partial fix that validates the name but keeps the reserved-prefix pass-through, or that keeps injecting system args before filtering, leaves this open.

injected sibling (shell branch): the invoking user's group membership is exposed to the main shell command template unvalidated. Reason to dismiss: it is a neighbouring identity field, not the login name the report points at; a verbatim reproduction of the published fix never touches it. INJECTED into our copy only.

injected sibling (direct-exec branch): the same group value is written into the environment of a direct-exec action (run without a shell). Reason to dismiss: direct-exec actions pass arguments as argv, so a solver may believe values on that branch cannot be injected and leaves its environment unhardened; the published fix never touches this branch. INJECTED into our copy only.
verified.project_tests_run: The project's own executor and config suites build and pass at the pinned+injected commit and on the oracle (go test ./internal/executor/ ./internal/config/, GOTOOLCHAIN=local GOFLAGS=-mod=mod CGO_ENABLED=0). The pinned commit does not contain the advisory's regression tests (the fix commit adds the shell_safe_identifier, reserved-prefix and filter-then-inject tests; at pinned the filter test asserts the vulnerable 'system args preserved' behaviour). Hidden suites: 4 security tests fail on pinned+injected and pass on the oracle; 6 functional cases pass on both. The injected siblings do not break any project test.

traps.shape: the published fix's protected sink: an identity-derived login name is substituted into the command OliveTin runs without a safety check
traps.where: service/internal/executor/executor.go:750-753 (injectSystemArgs), consumed at arguments.go parseActionArguments / executor.go stepExec
traps.reason_to_dismiss: none - this is the lead the report points at

traps.shape: allowlist bypass: an undeclared client argument with the reserved system prefix survives the filter and reaches the command environment
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a partial fix validates the login name but forgets to also drop the reserved-prefix pass-through and reorder injection after filtering

traps.shape: identity-field sibling: the invoking user's group membership is exposed to the main shell command template unvalidated
traps.reason_to_dismiss: it is a neighbouring identity field, not the login name the report flags; a verbatim reproduction of the published fix leaves it open
traps.realistic_because: a maintainer exposing the caller's group membership to action templates (as the login name already is) would write exactly this; INJECTED into our copy only, registered in build/audit/uncovered-routes.tsv

traps.shape: second execution branch: the same group value is written into the environment of a direct-exec action (run without a shell)
traps.reason_to_dismiss: direct-exec passes arguments as argv, so a solver may treat that branch as injection-proof and leave its environment unhardened; a different reason to skip than the shell-branch sibling
traps.realistic_because: the two execution branches are maintained separately; a maintainer adding the group exposure to both the shell and the direct-exec path, while the fix only hardens one, is realistic drift. INJECTED into our copy only, registered in build/audit/uncovered-routes.tsv

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the security tests assert no marker side effect; a panic or crash in the executor goroutine still leaves the marker absent but also fails the functional runs, so a crash cannot be scored as a clean refusal that passes
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: there is one protected operation - the command OliveTin runs and its environment - and no neighbouring or proxy resource a fix could authorise by mistake
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the sink is command execution; there is no read-vs-write distinction a fix could cover only one side of
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the correct guard checks the raw identity/argument value before it is templated or placed into the environment; there is no normalising step applied to the attacker value ahead of the check that a fix could be fooled by
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: the values are checked by allowed-character type, not parsed into identity fields, so there is no field-parsing mismatch a malformed spelling could slip past
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: safety is decided structurally from the value's characters; there is no external authority that could return empty and make the check fail open
wrong_fix_catalogue.adjacent_api: n/a: the fix is applied inside the executor's own argument handling; hardening.patch adds defence in depth to the shared environment builder without changing any API's stated behaviour, and the functional suite proves legitimate delivery still works

notes: Injected track. environment/inject.patch adds two sibling exposures to our copy only (the caller's group line templated into the shell command, and written into the direct-exec environment), applied at image build after checkout. Oracle = published source fix (drop the reserved-prefix pass-through in the argument filter; inject system args after filtering; validate the login name and tracking id as reserved system args; validate them again in the post-completion command path; reject config-declared reserved-prefix argument names) PLUS removal of both injected group exposures. The published post-completion command path (pattern-A far site in the upstream fix) is redundant for the login name here because the main-path validation already fails the request before the post-completion command runs; it is kept in the oracle for fidelity but is not a separately testable lever, so it is not a trap. Out of scope, noted not built: the post-completion command also templates the action's own stdout unvalidated (a different, second-order issue) and entity config data is templated unchecked (a different trust boundary).
